newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end flat, slight gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end flat, slight gains seen.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished flat to higher Tuesday after a quiet session with the U.S. Employment Cost Index figures release coming in as expected.
Traders predicted the market was most likely to rise gently in coming days until Friday's U.S. jobless report.
"The market was tranquil. It will rise slightly unless there are any upsetting economic indicators," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was flat at 95-1/4 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.1 to 118.70.
"The market is not yet ready for any bout of profit-taking," said another trader.
Apart from supportive domestic economic indicators the market continues to focus mainly on the U.S. Treasuries market, said traders.
In the money markets, three-month peso BAIBOR, the Buenos Aires interbank offered rate, fell to 6.56 percent from 6.75 percent.
